bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert a Contract Administrator Salary from Hourly to Annual

If you are a contract administrator or considering a role in this field, understanding how your hourly rate translates into an annual salary is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning your tax. This guide walks you through the conversion using a standard 38-hour week, explains the role of the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides, and shows how tax and the Medicare levy affect your take-home pay.

### The 38-Hour Week and the Fortnight

Most full-time contract administrators work 38 hours per week, which is the standard under many awards such as the Clerks Award. To calculate your annual gross salary, multiply your hourly rate by 38 and then by 52 weeks:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, a contract administrator on $35 per hour earns:

$35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160 per year

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is roughly $2,660 (weekly pay × 2). This figure helps you match your budget cycle. The calculator on this site uses the same formula and assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances – just the base rate repeated every week.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, contract administrators are usually covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, which include the correct classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check the relevant award before relying on a generic figure.

If you work as a casual contract administrator, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. For a $35 base rate, the casual rate becomes $43.75. The calculator has a checkbox to add this loading automatically – never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Figure

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

For a $69,160 annual salary, the tax is:

$4,020 + 0.30 × ($69,160 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $7,248 = $11,268

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For $69,160, that is $1,383. So total tax and Medicare is about $12,651, leaving a take-home pay of roughly $56,509 per year, or $4,709 per month.

Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles and families were not confirmed for 2026–27 in this estimate; the calculator uses the 2025–26 single thresholds. If you have a low income, you may be eligible for a reduction or exemption.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your gross pay. The maximum earnings that attract super is $270,830 per year. For a $69,160 salary, the super contribution is:

$69,160 × 0.12 = $8,299

This amount goes into your super fund and is taxed at 15% within the fund. The calculator shows super separately so you can see the total cost to your employer.

### Using the Pay and Conditions Tool

The Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool (PACT) provides award-specific rates, including penalty rates and allowances. If your contract administrator role involves shift work, overtime, or travel allowances, the tool can give a more accurate estimate than a simple hourly-to-annual conversion. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site also links to the latest National Minimum Wage and award rates.

### Annualised Wage Arrangements

Some employers pay contract administrators an annualised wage – a fixed amount that covers base pay, penalties, overtime, and allowances. Under the Clerks Award, for example, an annualised wage must be reviewed every 12 months to ensure the employee received at least what they would have earned under the award. If the annualised wage falls short, the employer must pay the difference. Always check your employment contract and the relevant award rules.

### Summary

Converting an hourly contract administrator salary to an annual figure is straightforward: multiply by 38 and by 52. But the real value depends on your award classification, casual or permanent status, and whether you receive penalty rates. Use the calculator on this site to enter your base hourly rate, add casual loading if applicable, and see your annual gross, tax, Medicare, and super. For a precise determination, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) and consult a tax professional.

Remember, the figures here are estimates. They assume a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, no salary sacrifice, and no HELP or Medicare levy surcharge. Your actual pay and tax may differ.
